steps.message:
Build an 8-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation titled "The Power of Vaccination: From Smallpox Eradication to COVID-19 in Record Time" for public health professionals and policy analysts. The tone should be data-forward, authoritative, and accessible.

The narrative arc begins with the accelerating pace of vaccine development over two centuries, moves through dramatic evidence of disease elimination and reduction in the US (including state-level measles data and the smallpox eradication story), explains the mechanism of herd immunity, then confronts remaining coverage gaps before closing with key takeaways and a call to action for global health systems.

For the "vaccine-timeline-acceleration" slide, use a horizontal bar chart showing the time span from pathogen identification to vaccine licensure for at least five diseases, with COVID-19's record timeline visually emphasized. For the "us-disease-elimination" slide, include a structured table comparing pre-vaccine annual case/death counts to current figures, clearly marking diseases with 100% reduction. The "measles-heatmap-states" slide should reference a heatmap-style visualization with annotated milestone years (1963, 1971, 1980). The "herd-immunity-mechanism" slide should include a simple diagram illustrating how population-level vaccination shields vulnerable individuals.

Do not fabricate data not found in source_brief.md. All statistics, percentages, and historical dates must be drawn directly from the provided brief.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

import collections 
import collections.abc
import pptx
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor

prs = pptx.Presentation()

# Set aspect ratio to 16:9
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Helper function to add a title
def add_title(slide, text):
    title = slide.shapes.title
    title.text = text
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(36)
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 51, 102)

# Slide 1: Title Slide
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0] # Title slide layout
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
title = slide.shapes.title
subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
title.text = "The Power of Vaccination: From Smallpox Eradication to COVID-19 in Record Time"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(48)
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 51, 102)
subtitle.text = "A data-driven overview of public health transformation (1796–2020)\nSource: Our World in Data"
subtitle.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(24)

# Slide 2: Vaccine Timeline Acceleration
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5] # Title only
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_title(slide, "From 100 Years to Under 1 Year: Vaccine Development Is Accelerating")

chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['COVID-19', 'Measles', 'Hepatitis B', 'Whooping cough', 'Ebola', 'Meningitis', 'Typhoid fever']
chart_data.add_series('Years from Pathogen ID to Vaccine Licensure', [0.8, 10, 16, 42, 43, 92, 105])

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(11), Inches(5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart

# Emphasize COVID-19
series = chart.series[0]
point = series.points[0]
point.format.fill.solid()
point.format.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 0, 0) # Red for emphasis

# Adding the image for reference as well
# slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg', Inches(7.5), Inches(2), height=Inches(3.5))

# Slide 3: US Disease Elimination
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_title(slide, "100% Case Reduction Achieved for Diphtheria, Polio, and Smallpox in the US")

rows = 10
cols = 6
left = Inches(0.5)
top = Inches(1.8)
width = Inches(12)
height = Inches(5)

table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table

headers = ["Disease", "Pre-Vaccine Cases\n(per mil/yr)", "Post-Vaccine Cases\n(per mil/yr)", "Case Reduction", "Pre-Vaccine Deaths\n(per mil/yr)", "Death Reduction"]
for col_idx, header_text in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0, col_idx)
    cell.text = header_text
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 51, 102)
    for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
        paragraph.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 255, 255)
        paragraph.font.bold = True
        paragraph.font.size = Pt(14)
        paragraph.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

data = [
    ["Diphtheria", "158", "0", "100%", "13.7", "100%"],
    ["Measles", "3,044", "0.2", "99.99%", "2.5", "100%"],
    ["Smallpox", "250", "0", "100%", "2.9", "100%"],
    ["Acute polio", "141", "0", "100%", "10", "100%"],
    ["Pertussis", "1,534", "52", "96.6%", "30.8", "99.7%"],
    ["Rubella", "242", "0.04", "99.98%", "0.09", "100%"],
    ["Hepatitis A", "465", "51", "89%", "0.5", "88.7%"],
    ["Acute hepatitis B", "273", "44", "83.9%", "1", "83.6%"],
    ["Pneumococcal", "233", "139", "40.5%", "24", "31.3%"]
]

for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data):
    for col_idx, cell_data in enumerate(row_data):
        cell = table.cell(row_idx + 1, col_idx)
        cell.text = cell_data
        for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
            paragraph.font.size = Pt(14)
            paragraph.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        # Highlight 100%
        if cell_data == "100%":
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(200, 255, 200)

# Slide 4: Measles Heatmap States
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_title(slide, "Measles Cases Collapsed Across All 50 US States After Vaccine Mandates")

slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg', Inches(0.5), Inches(1.8), height=Inches(5.2))

# Add annotations
txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(9.5), Inches(2), Inches(3.5), Inches(1))
tf = txbox.text_frame
tf.text = "1963: First measles vaccine"
tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
tf.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(153, 0, 0)

txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(9.5), Inches(3.5), Inches(3.5), Inches(1))
tf = txbox.text_frame
tf.text = "1971: MMR vaccine introduced"
tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
tf.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(153, 0, 0)

txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(9.5), Inches(5), Inches(3.5), Inches(1))
tf = txbox.text_frame
tf.text = "1980: Mandated for kindergarten"
tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
tf.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(153, 0, 0)

# Slide 5: Smallpox Eradication
slide_layout_bullet = prs.slide_layouts[1] # Title and Content
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout_bullet)
add_title(slide, "Smallpox: The Only Human Disease Eradicated Through Vaccination")

tf = slide.shapes.placeholders[1].text_frame
tf.text = "The Greatest Vaccination Success Story"
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "1959: WHO passes resolution to eradicate smallpox globally."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "1967: Intensified eradication campaign launched."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "1977: The last natural case occurred in Somalia."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "1980: Smallpox certified eradicated worldwide."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Why smallpox was suited for eradication:"
p.level = 0
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Infected only humans (no animal reservoirs)."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Symptoms were clearly distinguishable."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "The vaccine was cheap, effective, and stable."
p.level = 1

# Slide 6: Herd Immunity
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_title(slide, "Herd Immunity: How Vaccinating Many Protects the Most Vulnerable")

# Diagram for Herd Immunity
# Add a few circles
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE

# Vaccinated
slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(2), Inches(3), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5)).fill.solid()
slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(2.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5)).fill.solid()
slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(3.5), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5)).fill.solid()
slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(4), Inches(2), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5)).fill.solid()
slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(5), Inches(3), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5)).fill.solid()

# Give them colors
for shape in slide.shapes:
    if shape.has_text_frame == False and shape.shape_type == 1:
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 153, 0) # Green for vaccinated

# Vulnerable
vul1 = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(3.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5))
vul1.fill.solid()
vul1.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 0, 0) # Red for vulnerable

vul2 = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(2.5), Inches(4), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5))
vul2.fill.solid()
vul2.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 0, 0)

# Unvaccinated / Pathogen source
path1 = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(0.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5))
path1.fill.solid()
path1.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(100, 100, 100) # Gray for pathogen source

# Adding Legend / Labels
txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(6), Inches(2.5), Inches(5), Inches(2))
tf = txbox.text_frame
tf.text = "How it works:"
tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
tf.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(24)

p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Green: Vaccinated individuals forming a barrier."
p.font.size = Pt(18)
p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 153, 0)

p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Red: Vulnerable individuals (newborns, immunocompromised, cancer patients)."
p.font.size = Pt(18)
p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 0, 0)

p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "When enough people are vaccinated, pathogens cannot spread effectively, shielding those who cannot be vaccinated."
p.font.size = Pt(18)

# Slide 7: Remaining Challenges
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout_bullet)
add_title(slide, "Gaps Persist: Pneumococcal Disease Shows Only 40% Case Reduction")

tf = slide.shapes.placeholders[1].text_frame
tf.text = "Vaccine impact is still incomplete for some diseases:"
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Pneumococcal Disease: 40.5% case reduction, 31.3% death reduction."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Hepatitis A: 89% case reduction, 88.7% death reduction."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Acute Hepatitis B: 83.9% case reduction, 83.6% death reduction."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Barriers to complete control:"
p.level = 0
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Global access gaps: Not everyone has access to life-saving vaccines."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Supply shortages: Putting children in many regions at risk."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Trust challenges: Poor scientific understanding reduces uptake and herd immunity."
p.level = 1

# Slide 8: Key Takeaways
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout_bullet)
add_title(slide, "Key Takeaways: Vaccines Have Eliminated Deadly Diseases — But the Job Isn't Done")

tf = slide.shapes.placeholders[1].text_frame
tf.text = "Summary of Impact and Future Priorities:"
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "100% Elimination Achieved: Diphtheria, smallpox, and both forms of polio have been eradicated in the US."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Timelines Collapsed: Vaccine development dropped from >100 years to <1 year, driven by mRNA and genomic tools."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Herd Immunity Works: Broad vaccination coverage effectively protects entire communities."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Persisting Coverage Gaps: Diseases like pneumococcal disease and hepatitis A/B highlight ongoing challenges."
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Call to Action: We must improve global access, ensure steady supply, and build trust to finish the job."
p.level = 1
p.font.bold = True
p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 51, 102)

prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
print("Presentation generated successfully at /app/output/final_deck.pptx")
